findings:
🟠 [test-base-copy-in-checkout] MUST-FIX hooks/tests/dispatch-review-blind-kimi-agy.test.sh writes its base-script copy to `$REPO_ROOT/scripts/.dispatch-review-base-$$.sh`, i.e. into the checkout, and the `rm -f` sits only inside the success branch of `if git show 47a0e1c6:… > "$BASE_COPY"`. When that branch-internal SHA is unreachable (squash-merge, gc, shallow clone) the redirect has already created an empty file that is never removed, so every run leaves a stray untracked file in scripts/ and the non-blind byte-compare is silently skipped. Impact: violates spec §2.5 (tests never touch the main checkout) and §5 (fixtures only under a temp dir), and the phase-3 "non-blind byte-for-byte" proof can go vacuous without a failure. Smallest remediation: build the base copy under `$TEST_TMP` (a scripts/ dir with `lib` linked or copied, as cleanroom-launch-kimi-agy.test.sh already does for the base launcher), or at minimum remove the file on the failure path and report the skip loudly.
Minor [changelog-missing] MUST-FIX The spec file map (§3) and phase 5 both list `CHANGELOG.md` as a deliverable, and §2.6 declares a `published-compatible` behaviour change (kimi/agy panels now admitted on a green probe; refusal text changed). The diff has no CHANGELOG.md hunk and the reviewer notes do not declare it deferred. Impact: the user-visible admission change ships unrecorded. Smallest remediation: add one CHANGELOG entry covering kimi/agy cleanroom tier, the per-runner probe, and the advisory version warning.
Minor [portability-doc-stale-agy] MUST-FIX `references/multi-agent-portability.md` and its `platforms/codex/plugin/references/` mirror state that the agy 1.2.15 live-fire "produced no verdict; cause not yet diagnosed". The same diff's `references/blind-dispatch.md` and the `live-fire/agy-rerun/` receipts show the cause diagnosed (config/agents migration, dangling symlink), repaired, and the rerun `reviewed`. Impact: the phase-5 "facts" reference contradicts the shipped behaviour and tells operators the agy seat does not work. Smallest remediation: replace that sentence in both copies with the diagnosed cause, the repair, and the rerun result.
🔵 [blind-fallthrough-guard] CUT/FOLLOW-UP In `scripts/dispatch-review.sh` a blind kimi/agy call whose packet dir is set but incomplete falls through to the pre-existing codex `cleanroom)` tier case, which the diff does not show. A one-line guard in the kimi and agy branches (blind=1 and `BLIND_RUNNER_CLEANROOM`=0 → `die_precondition`) would make it structurally impossible to reach the tooled non-blind argv under blind mode. Excluded: no concrete failure is demonstrable from the diff and the no-packet case is tested as refused.
🔵 [engine-rail-e2e-unverified] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Three things rest on code outside the diff: that `campaignControl` is in scope at both `cleanroomExpectedVersions(campaignControl)` call sites in `src/engine/autopilot-engine.js`; that `prepareReviewLaunch` exports `AUTOPILOT_REVIEW_PACKET_DIR` for kimi/agy and not only codex; and that the blind agy branch's `--model "$MODEL"` carries the resolved alias. The live-fire drove `dispatch-review.sh` directly with a concrete model id. One engine-level test (`prepareReviewLaunch` with runner kimi/agy plus a packet asserts the env var) would close the "intake admits a seat the rail cannot run" risk. Excluded: no failure is observable from the diff.
🔵 [agy-marker-agent-false] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The cleanroom agy audit requires an `agent=true` line and no not-found line, but does not breach on an additional `Starting new conversation (agent=false)` or `agentScript=false` line. Likewise the kimi audit keeps only the last `profile.bind` and ignores a non-empty `activeToolNames`. Excluded: a single `-p` run starts one conversation, and the tool-snapshot and transcript checks still void any real tool use.
🔵 [kimi-node-dir-breadth] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `cleanroom-launch.sh` binds `dirname(dirname(node))` read-only at /opt/node. An unusual install (node at `$HOME/bin/node`, or a prefix holding `etc/npmrc`) would expose that tree inside the seat, and the deny-path probe checks host paths, not the /opt/node alias. Excluded: not the case on the probed host, and the seat agent is tool-less with the audit deciding; a later refusal when NODE_DIR equals or contains a deny path would be cheap.
🔵 [phase5-negative-control-receipt] CUT/FOLLOW-UP No committed receipt exists for the phase-5 sabotaged-agent live negative control. Excluded: the host-gated real-kimi preflight test refuses an agent file without `description`, and the first agy live-fire is itself a real audit-voided `no_verdict` run.
